value.rationale: The specific recent practical method uses A_c=I without an exact discrete analysis. The negative theorem shows a basis-dependent universal impossibility on natural, nonsingular symmetric indefinite bilinear games (even though these games are isometrically equivalent to stable all-positive instances), not merely an isolated numerical divergence. The complementary aligned correction and sharp two-regime fixed-gain optimizer identify how coupling geometry, singular-value spread, and residual rotational gain determine feasible and optimal learning rates, enabling quantitative algorithm design; this is more than a trivial sign check.
